Population increased in Chorley

The estimated population of Chorley in 2024 was 120,839 usual residents, a rise of 0.8% since 2023.

This meant that Chorley's rate of population change placed it about average among local authority districts in England and Wales.

In the period from mid-2021 to mid-2024, the population estimate of Chorley increased by 2.5%.

Over this slightly longer period, Chorley was also among the areas that had a broadly average population increase, of local authority districts in England and Wales.

Age profile of Chorley

The average (median) age stayed at 43.8 years between 2023 and 2024.

You can see how the age profile of Chorley has changed since 2011 in the population pyramid below.

sections.content:
Chorley is an area that is classed as intermediate rural in nature according to the 2021 Census Rural Urban Classification.

By age category, Chorley's population of 120,839 usual residents was made up of:

  • 21,258 people aged 0 to 15 years, (17.6%)
  • 74,304 people aged 16 to 64 years, (61.5%)
  • 25,277 people aged 65 years and over, (20.9%)

    • Compared with England and Wales as a whole, Chorley has a slightly higher proportion of people aged 65 years and over (20.9% compared with 18.9% for England and Wales).

Contributors to population change

We look at different flows of people into and out of areas and births and deaths to see what is driving population change in each area.

In Chorley, the largest contribution to population change in the year to mid-2024 was from net internal migration.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Chorley
sections.subtitle: How the population changed, by component

sections.content:
We estimate that, for Chorley, between 2023 and 2024:

  • More deaths than births led to a fall in the population of 364 people (-0.3%). In total, there were 976 births and 1,340 deaths in Chorley.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other areas in the UK) increased the population by 887 (0.7%). There were 6,341 people entering the area and 5,454 people leaving the area.
  • Net international migration led to an increase in Chorley's population of 496 (0.4%) as a result of 697 people entering the area and 201 people leaving the area.
  • Other change (which includes changes to armed forces personnel and prisoners) for Chorley was less than 0.1%.

Revisions to 2023 population estimates

We regularly revise our initial population estimates as we get more data and methods improve.

Our revised estimate for the population of Chorley in mid-2023 is 119,823.

Within this, international migration was revised upwards by 249 people and internal migration estimates were revised upwards by 222 people.

Overall, there was an revision upwards of 471 people.
